one_line: Sanskrit physician-scholar of Kashmir who restored and completed the Charaka Saṃhitā in the early medieval period.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his late 30s to early 40s, lean scholar’s build with a slightly stooped posture from long hours of study.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, observant gaze; medium Kashmiri brown complexion; straight nose, neat trimmed moustache and short beard along the jawline; a thin vertical tilak of pale sandalwood on the forehead; default expression is thoughtful, gentle but firm, as if weighing a difficult medical decision.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair pulled back into a modest topknot at the crown, with the rest tied into a low, neat bun; a narrow off‑white cloth headband wraps around the forehead and under the knot, keeping stray hair back.
appearance.costume: He wears an 8th–9th century Kashmiri brahmin physician’s attire: a full‑sleeved, knee-length off‑white cotton kurta with a simple round collar and side ties; over it a soft, deep saffron woollen uttariya/shawl draped from the left shoulder across the torso and wrapped around the back, its border edged with a narrow maroon stripe; below, a plain unpatterned dull‑ochre cotton dhoti tied securely at the waist and pleated to mid-calf, always drawn to cover the legs fully; on his feet, simple dark brown leather sandals; around his neck, a single tulsi bead mala and a small copper amulet cylinder; his right wrist bears a plain wooden bracelet, and he carries a small cloth belt‑pouch at his back for herbs and writing tools.
appearance.signature: A tightly bound palm‑leaf manuscript bundle of the Charaka Saṃhitā, wrapped in a reddish-brown cloth with two horizontal wooden boards and knotted cords, always held in his left arm, with a short iron stylus and a small round ink pot hanging from the bundle by a thin cord.

ref_desc: Dṛḍhabala is a lean Kashmiri scholar with medium brown skin, black hair in a topknot and headband, an off-white kurta, dull-ochre dhoti, deep saffron shawl, simple beads and sandals, always carrying a cloth-wrapped palm-leaf Charaka Saṃhitā bundle with stylus and ink pot in warm earth tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Dṛḍhabala of Kashmir: a lean, late-30s to early-40s Sanskrit physician-scholar with medium Kashmiri brown skin, an oval thoughtful face, neat moustache and short jawline beard, and a thin vertical sandalwood tilak on his forehead. His thick black hair is pulled into a modest topknot at the crown with the rest tied into a low bun, held back by a narrow off-white cloth headband. He wears a long-sleeved, knee-length off-white cotton kurta with a plain round collar and side ties, over a fully covering dull-ochre cotton dhoti pleated to mid-calf, and on top a deep saffron woollen uttariya/shawl draped from his left shoulder across his torso and around his back, bordered with a narrow maroon stripe. His feet have simple dark brown leather sandals; around his neck is a single tulsi bead mala and a small copper amulet cylinder, with a plain wooden bracelet on his right wrist and a small cloth belt-pouch at his back. In his left arm he always cradles a tightly bound palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Charaka Saṃhitā wrapped in reddish-brown cloth between two wooden boards, its cords tied securely, with a short iron stylus and a small round ink pot hanging from the bundle by a thin cord. Use a palette of off-white, deep saffron, dull ochre, maroon, and dark brown, and show front, side, and back views that clearly display his consistent face, hair arrangement, garments, accessories, and the manuscript bundle as his constant prop.
